seriesStmt.p: Machine readable texts of the unpublished correspondence of James Joyce

projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

div.p:
First of all thanks for your efforts to find a photograph of the Kensington Tapestry. My father thanks you for the Degas picture which I have just pasted into the operatic score. You will receive a letter by next post from Mr. Léon. Meanwhile my father asks me to send you the following replies: Tenors This article by count Carducci appeared in the english English quarterly Music and Letters. Miss Weaver will be able to give you the exact date. Fedora The tenor Romanza in this opera is called Amor ti vieta . The words are: Amor ti vieta di non amar la man tua lieve che mi respinge
di The atonic vowel should come in the last word between the two final consonants.

Chapelizod My father does not know whether you can still have access to the River river through the grounds of the former Distillery distillery in which my grandfather was secretary and shareholder. It is on the left of the main Street street on the right bank of the River river as you go upstream but if not a view from the Bridge bridge or possibly from the other bank under the Hamlet hamlet which used to be called Fox and Geese, would do. The principal bistro, he says, was the Mullingar Inn, of which in W.i.P. the big man is assumed to be landlord. He thinks you should ask your friend in Dublin Dr. Liebmann to obtain for you from the publishers Duffy and Son a copy of
The Old House by the Churchyard
, alluded to in the last fragment in Transition, see paragraph beginning it darkles, an old fashioned novel about Chapelizod written by Sheridan Le Fanu probably an irish Irish Huguenot of whom there were many in Dublin where they founded, I mean the Huguenots the irish Irish
Paplin poplin industry. Wetherup My father would be very much intrigued to see a picture of this nobleman’s backdoor and it would be probably very true to life if it had a notice to quit nailed upon it.
Dublin if you go there over Easter Monday he says you ought to go by bus to the Dargle and be very careful of the wheels coming back.

You will be glad to hear that my letters for Chaucer’s A.B.C. Poem have been accepted by Burns and Oats Oates and it is probable that a preface will be written by Mr. Louis Gillet who is at present curator of the Abbey, now a national museum, in which the french French monk wrote the original of it. Introductions My father has been so long absent from Dublin and has so little trust in people there that he hesitates in this matter but Mr. Leon Léon will write to you on the subject to-morrow.

div.note: Edgardo Carducci, “The Tenor Voice in Europe”, Music and Letters, Vol. 11 No. 4, October 1930, pp. 318-324.

Umberto Giordano's opera Fedora, dramma di V. Sardou (Milan: Sonzogno, 1898). The quotation here is from act 2, scene 8, in which tenor Count Loris Ipanov is flirting with soprano Princess Fedora Romanzov. Budgen quotes JJ on the lyrics: “It would be impossible to sing that 'respinge' without interpolating a vowel breath between the 'n' and the 'g'.” (JJMU 18)

Budgen was planning a trip to visit sites associated with Ulysses and Finnegans Wake, and travelled to the area later in April 1933. The Phoenix Park Distillery had closed by that time. The Mullingar Inn is the realistic setting for Finnegans Wake; “the big man” is the book's character H.C.E.

Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu's The House by the Churchyard (Dublin: James Duffy; London: Macmillan, 1899). The book appears multiple times in Finnegans Wake, and Budgen mentions it in JJMU (310). “It darkles”, FW 244.13.
Le Fanu was indeed a Huguenot, a son of a Church of Ireland clergyman. In “Cyclops”, the Citizen's enumeration of Irish industries includes “our Huguenot poplin” (U 12.1245).

Known to Leopold Bloom and mentioned in Ulysses (7:337, 7:342-43; 16:1701). An acquaintance of JJ's father, in and out of debt, which is probably what JJ refers to regarding a notice to leave the premises attached to his back door. See JJ Online Notes. Wetherup is mentioned in JJMU (290).
Budgen travelled to Dublin for research on JJMU in April 1933. The Dargle is a picturesque mountain glen not far from Dublin.

The book with Lucia Joyce's illuminated letters was eventually published in 1936: A Chaucer A.B.C., Being a Hymn to the Holy Virgin in an English Version...from the French of Guillaume de Deguilleville, Initial Letters Designed and Illuminated by Lucia Joyce (Paris: Obelisk Press, 1936).
